There's the PayPal Mafia, and then there is the DPS RK Puram Mafia,

Another addition with a $500M ARR giant:

> be Rohan Nayak
> spawn in Delhi
> study at DPS RK Puram (mafia loading)
> ace bachelors at IIT Kharagpur
> dive into corporate finance at Credit Suisse
> switch to Paytm as PM
> spend hours commuting between Gurgaon and Delhi
> audiobooks and podcasts to kill time
> eventually get bored of them too
> notices zero good serialized audio content

2018
> quit Paytm to start Pocket FM
> idea: build an audio entertainment platform
> investors aren't convinced
> users aren't convinced either
> try 11 different formats
> barely 10,000 downloads
> nearly run out of money

2019-2020
> finally discover serialized fiction
> 10-minute episodes + cliffhangers
> daily listening jumps from ~25m to 2h+
> finally find product-market fit

2021-2023
> introduce microtransactions
> pivots hard into the US market
> culturally localize stories instead of translating them
> US becomes 70% of revenue
> raise $65M Series C
> valuation jumps to $390 million
> revenue compounds, hits $150M ARR
> Fortune India 40 Under 40
> 70% of revenue comes from America
> raise $103M Series D
> valuation nearly doubles to $750M

2025
> realize humans can't produce enough content
> go all-in on AI
> content production explodes
> goes from ~25K hours → 2.5M+
> generate ~10K AI marketing videos/month
> paid retention goes 35% → 60%
> add $250M+ net-new ARR

2026
> 250M+ listeners globally
> 500,000+ people writing on the platform
> many started as Pocket FM listeners
> 70% of revenue from the US
> ~$500M ARR

from: 10,000 downloads, 11 failed formats, and nearly running out of money

to: 250M+ listeners and ~$500M ARR

All because one guy got bored on the metro.

He didn't win by getting the idea right. He won by trying 11 versions until he found the one people couldn't stop listening to.

Rohan Nayak for you, ladies and gentlemen.

2089793870876061901.text:
> be Navneet Dalal
> spawn in Chandigarh, India
> do your engineering degree at NSIT, Delhi
> grind two years in Indian software firms
> get bored, fly to France 
> do a PhD on a problem most people call unsolvable
> "teach a machine to find a human being in an image"
> don't just improve the state of the art
> beat it by 100 to 1000x
> publish it in 2005
> call it Histograms of Oriented Gradients
> watch it become THE standard for a decade
> 25,000+ citations
> every pedestrian-detection system on earth ends up running your work
> a car brakes for someone in a crosswalk? that's your math
> ...this is still just the PhD
> not enough

> co-found a webcam startup that reads hand gestures, 2011, no cloud, runs on the device
> Apple names it App of the Year
> rank #1 in 72 countries
> Google tests it against their OWN algorithms
> yours wins
> Google buys the whole company for $40M
> go run the vision behind Nest's cameras 
> installed in millions of homes
> ...you are now, by any measure, at the top of the entire field
> could name your price at any AI lab on earth

> the man who built the iPod personally tells you not to do your next idea
> do it anyway
> disappear into 9 years on the single unsexiest machine in the house
> refuse the LiDAR crutch everyone else bolts on
> teach a robot to see a cluttered home the way your paper taught cars to see people
> sock, cable, dog, spill, all understood, all handled, in real time
> run all of it on a chip inside the robot so nothing ever leaves the house

> ship Matic
> WIRED 10/10. Benioff buys one.
> everyone in AI is racing to build a mind
> you spent 9 years on the quieter, harder thing
> a machine that truly sees a living room
> "he lost it" → "he saw it first"

> tatas fund it
> still runs today
> pattern's set: never gives up
> build the biggest version of wherever he failed at first
> spend 6 years learning supply chains cold

> claims to wire you $10k if they can't find $500k in waste

What’s your excuse?
